overview: Quantitative assessment of genomic database completeness against environmental microbial diversity

environmental_baseline.description: Ground truth environmental diversity from rRNA gene surveys
environmental_baseline.initial_format: Raw sequence data clustered into OTUs

key_metrics.otu_count: Number of unique OTU clusters per taxon
key_metrics.size_count: Total sequence abundance (read count) per taxon

key_metrics.otu_count: Number of unique OTU clusters per taxon
key_metrics.size_count: Total sequence abundance (read count) per taxon

environmental_baseline.processing_notes: OTUs represent species-level diversity; each OTU is a proxy for a distinct species in the environment

genomic_databases.description: Reference genomic databases with sequenced organisms
genomic_databases.species_subsetting: Genomes grouped by species-level taxid to prevent strain-level inflation

GTDB.description: Genome Taxonomy Database - curated prokaryotic genomes with standardized taxonomy
GTDB.species_subsetting: Aggregated to species using GTDB species representatives
GTDB.taxonomic_parsing: Parsed by phylum, family, genus using taxonkit and lineage functions
GTDB.domain_filtering: Prokaryotes only - Bacteria and Archaea domains
GTDB.coverage_note: GTDB is completely covered by NCBI (validated through comparison pipeline)
GTDB.validation: GTDB-NCBI comparison pipeline proves complete overlap and validates matching algorithms

NCBI.description: NCBI GenBank - comprehensive genome collection across all domains of life
NCBI.species_subsetting: Grouped by species-level taxid to get unique species count
NCBI.taxonomic_parsing: Parsed by phylum, family, genus using taxonkit lineage functions with domain-specific aggregation

aggregation_metrics.total_genome_count: Sum of all genome assemblies per taxon per domain
aggregation_metrics.species_count: Unique species-level taxids per taxon per domain
aggregation_metrics.domain_subset_counts: Separate counts for Bacteria, Archaea, Eukaryota

NCBI.tools_used: taxonkit for taxonomic lineage retrieval and parsing
NCBI.additional_metrics: Isolate vs MAG classification, assembly level tracking

genomic_databases.processing_notes: Critical: Species-level taxid subsetting prevents artificial inflation from multiple strains of same species
genomic_databases.database_relationship: GTDB (prokaryotes only) is completely covered by NCBI; NCBI provides universal coverage across all domains

step_1_environmental_parsing.description: Parse and aggregate environmental census data by taxonomic rank
process: Clean taxonomic names (remove organellar sequences, handle Candidatus)
Extract appropriate taxonomic rank (genus from species, etc.)
Aggregate OTU counts and size counts by rank
Retrieve full taxonomic lineages using taxonkit

step_2_genomic_parsing.description: Parse genomic databases from strain-level to species-aggregated taxonomic ranks
process: Filter by domain (Bacteria/Archaea for prokaryotes, Eukaryota for eukaryotes)
Count unique species per taxon (prevents strain inflation)
step_2_genomic_parsing.critical_note: Species subsetting is essential - without it, 100 E. coli strains would falsely appear as 100 species

step_3_domain_separation.description: Separate prokaryotic and eukaryotic data streams for domain-specific comparisons

matching_algorithms.overview: Custom-designed hierarchical matching system for linking environmental taxa to genomic databases
matching_algorithms.innovation: Novel multi-tier matching algorithm perfected through GTDB-NCBI validation pipeline
matching_algorithms.validation_note: Matching algorithms were developed and validated through comprehensive GTDB-NCBI comparison, proving complete database overlap

tier_1_taxid_matching.description: NCBI Taxonomy ID-based hierarchical matching - the gold standard
tier_1_taxid_matching.algorithm: Direct taxid comparison between census and genomic data with hierarchical aggregation
advantages: Handles taxonomic name changes and synonyms automatically
Most reliable and accurate matching method
Immune to spelling variations and database inconsistencies
Captures hierarchical relationships through lineage traversal
Primary method - achieves majority of matches
tier_1_taxid_matching.match_percentage: ~85-90% of all matches achieved through taxid matching
tier_1_taxid_matching.why_primary: Taxid matching is the most effective because it uses stable numeric identifiers that persist across name changes and database updates

tier_2_vectorized_lineage_matching.description: Regex-based lineage string matching - handles misnaming and database inconsistencies
tier_2_vectorized_lineage_matching.algorithm: Pattern matching within semicolon-delimited lineage strings using taxonkit-generated lineages
advantages: Handles misnaming across databases (e.g., GTDB vs NCBI naming differences)
Vectorized pandas operations for speed - 4x faster than iterative matching
Catches taxa missed by taxid matching due to database inconsistencies

tier_3_direct_name_matching.description: Exact string comparison - final fallback for edge cases
limitations: Rarely needed after taxid and lineage matching

tier_4_hierarchical_aggregation.description: Aggregate all descendant genomes for a given taxon
tier_4_hierarchical_aggregation.algorithm: Sum genome/species counts for all lineage matches

example.aggregation: Sum all genomes/species from all descendants

match_classification.direct_match: Exact name match at same taxonomic level

match_status_categories.matched: Environmental taxon found in genomic database
match_status_categories.census_only: Environmental taxon NOT in genomic database (novel diversity)
match_status_categories.db_only: Genomic taxon NOT in environmental census (rare/absent in samples)

performance_optimization.vectorization: Pandas string operations instead of Python loops
performance_optimization.scalability: Handles 287K environmental taxa vs 2.9M genomes efficiently

comparison_metrics.overview: Comprehensive metrics quantifying environmental diversity vs genomic representation

category_1_abundance_metrics.description: Environmental diversity and abundance from census data

census_otu_count.definition: Number of unique OTU clusters for this taxon
census_otu_count.interpretation: Proxy for species-level diversity in environment
census_otu_count.example: Proteobacteria: 50,000 OTUs = ~50,000 distinct species in environment

census_size_count.definition: Total sequence abundance (read count) for this taxon
census_size_count.interpretation: Proxy for relative abundance in environmental samples

otu_percentage.example: Proteobacteria: 17.4% = represents 17.4% of all prokaryotic diversity

ncbi_genome_count.definition: Total number of genome assemblies for this taxon
ncbi_genome_count.note: Includes multiple strains of same species

ncbi_species_count.definition: Number of unique species (by species-level taxid) for this taxon
ncbi_species_count.example: Proteobacteria: 25,000 unique species (100 E. coli strains = 1 species)
ncbi_species_count.interpretation: Comparable to census_otu_count for diversity comparison

isolate_count.definition: Number of genomes from cultured isolates (vs MAGs)

genome_pct_db.interpretation: Proportion of database devoted to this taxon
genome_pct_db.example: Proteobacteria: 51.7% = over half of all prokaryotic genomes

category_3_analytical_metrics.description: KEY COINED METRICS - Novel analytical metrics introduced in this study
category_3_analytical_metrics.note: These metrics are original contributions coined in this paper for quantifying database completeness

novelty_factor.status: 🔴 COINED METRIC - Primary contribution of this study
novelty_factor.interpretation: Environmental diversity relative to genomic representation
novelty_factor.meaning: How many environmental OTUs exist per sequenced species - CULTIVATION GAP INDICATOR
novelty_factor.significance: Quantifies the magnitude of missing genomic representation for environmental diversity

thresholds.infinity: ∞ - Taxa in environment but ZERO genomes in database

example.interpretation: 2.77× more environmental diversity than genomic data - significant cultivation gap

novelty_factor.research_application: Identifies high-priority taxa for genome sequencing efforts

overrepresentation_factor.status: 🔵 COINED METRIC - Secondary contribution of this study
overrepresentation_factor.interpretation: Genomic representation relative to environmental diversity
overrepresentation_factor.meaning: How many sequenced species exist per environmental OTU - DATABASE BIAS INDICATOR
overrepresentation_factor.significance: Reveals systematic biases toward easily cultured or model organisms

thresholds.high_overrepresentation: >2 - Database bias toward easily cultured taxa

example.interpretation: Many genomes/species but few environmental OTUs - research bias toward culturable taxa

overrepresentation_factor.research_application: Identifies overrepresented taxa that dominate databases despite low environmental abundance

values.matched: Environmental taxon found in genomic database
values.census_only: Environmental taxon NOT in database - NOVEL DIVERSITY
values.db_only: Database taxon NOT in environmental samples - rare/absent

research_significance.census_only_taxa: Cultivation priorities - these taxa need genome sequencing
research_significance.matched_taxa: Compare novelty factors to identify underrepresented groups
research_significance.db_only_taxa: Rare taxa or sampling bias indicators

direct_matches.definition: Number of exact name matches at same taxonomic level

total_matches.interpretation: Total genomic entries matched to this environmental taxon

merged_comparison_files.description: Final merged datasets combining environmental and genomic data
